key_insight: Finite feasibility is not enough: shallow constrained QAOA can only access a finite-depth subset of feasible states, and that accessible subset better predicts performance than feasibility alone.
engineering_relevance: For resource-bounded quantum optimization, the paper provides a practical diagnostic to compare mixer schedules by both reachable volume and objective quality before running expensive circuits.
method: Define the finite-depth accessible set R_p(M,x0) for a specific feasible start state, mixer schedule, and circuit depth.
Derive an objective ceiling f_R^* and normalized reachable-quality metric Q_R from the accessible set.
Test resource-matched block-local XY mixer schedules on constrained portfolio optimization and synthetic block-constrained quadratic problems.
evidence_signal: Across 207 favorable-tail CVaR QAOA configurations, Q_R showed the strongest association with realized shallow-QAOA performance, with Pearson 0.7003 and Spearman 0.8057 correlations.
watch_item: The diagnostic is circuit- and schedule-specific, so its usefulness depends on accurately modeling the implemented mixer order, initialization, and compilation effects.
paper_title: Beyond Feasibility: Finite-Depth Accessibility in Constrained QAOA
